Package frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.module

Class SwerveModuleIOReal

java.lang.Object
frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.module.SwerveModuleIOReal
All Implemented Interfaces:
SwerveModuleIO
public class SwerveModuleIOReal extends Object implements SwerveModuleIO
SwerveModuleIO implementation for a real swerve module driven by Controller-based drive/steer motors and a CTRE CANCoder absolute encoder.

  • Constructor Details

    • SwerveModuleIOReal

      public SwerveModuleIOReal(SwerveModuleConstants constants, SwerveConstants swerveConstants)
      Constructs the module's drive/steer controllers and CANCoder from the given constants, and registers their position signals with the OdometryThread when swerveConstants.special.enableOdometryThread is set and both motors are TalonFX-controlled.
      Parameters:
      constants - this module's specific IDs, inversions and CANCoder offset
      swerveConstants - the shared swerve constants (motor types, CAN bus, odometry settings, etc.)

  • Method Details

    • setDesiredState

      public void setDesiredState(edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModuleState desiredState, boolean isOpenLoop, boolean preventJittering)
      Commands the module towards the given state, closing the loop on drive velocity unless isOpenLoop is set.
      Specified by:
      setDesiredState in interface SwerveModuleIO
      Parameters:
      desiredState - the target module speed and angle (not necessarily optimized yet; implementations are expected to optimize it against the current module angle)
      isOpenLoop - if true, drive the wheel by voltage/percent output instead of a velocity control loop
      preventJittering - if true, hold the last commanded angle instead of rotating the module when the requested speed is near zero, to avoid wheel jitter

    • resetToAbsolute

      public void resetToAbsolute()
      Re-seeds the steer motor's relative encoder from the CANCoder's absolute position, wrapped to [-pi, pi). Use this to recover a correct steer angle after a brownout or power cycle without re-homing the module by hand.

    • update

      public SwerveModuleIO.SwerveModuleIOInputs update()
      Reads the current module state and returns a fresh SwerveModuleIO.SwerveModuleIOInputs. Should be called once per robot loop cycle.

      The absolute CANCoder position is only re-read every 10 calls (cached otherwise), since CAN reads of it are comparatively expensive.

      Specified by:
      update in interface SwerveModuleIO
      Returns:
      the latest module readings

    • periodic

      public void periodic()
      Runs any per-cycle module control-loop updates that are not tied to a new SwerveModuleIO.setDesiredState(edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModuleState, boolean, boolean) call (e.g. re-applying the last commanded output). Should be called once per robot loop cycle. Delegates to the drive and steer Controllers' own periodic updates.
      Specified by:
      periodic in interface SwerveModuleIO
